title: The gradient is perpendicular to the level curve
caption: For f = x²y + y³ at (1, 1), ∇f = (2xy, x² + 3y²) = (2, 4). The tangent line to the level curve there is 2(x − 1) + 4(y − 1) = 0, i.e. x + 2y = 3, with direction (2, −1); (2, 4) · (2, −1) = 0, so the gradient points straight across the contour, uphill.
alt: From (1, 1) an arrow along the gradient (2, 4) and a dashed tangent line x + 2y = 3 with direction (2, −1), at a right angle.
description: The tangent to the level curve is x + 2y = 3, direction (2, −1), since 2 × 2 + 4 × (−1) = 0.
So the gradient is normal to the level curve and points in the direction of steepest increase.
